If you work alone, you do not need a workflow: a habit, a goal or [Autopilot](/guide/ai-tasks) covers a personal routine. A single quest with no team can still have a workflow on its quest page.

## Where to find Workflows

- Open the menu (the hamburger icon), expand **AI Productivity**, then tap **Workflows**. The same entry is on your Profile page under AI Productivity.
- On a team's page, tap the **Workflows** row ("Who does what, and when, as a diagram"). It opens the same screen with that team already selected.
- On an organization's page, the same **Workflows** row opens the screen with that organization selected.

Like the rest of AI Productivity, Workflows works during the 31-day Quest AI trial and on the paid plans. On the Free plan the page shows what you get and a **Subscribe** button instead. Whatever you built stays, as with the rest of Quest. See [Plans](/reference/plans).

## Start a workflow

Tap **New workflow** in the switcher, or the button in an empty list. Give it a name, choose the team or organization it is for, and start in one of four ways:

- **Describe it and let AI draft it**: say what the workflow is for and who is involved. The AI drafts it, you see the draft as a diagram marked "Draft, not live yet", and you can ask for changes ("make the reply due sooner"). Each request is saved in a feedback history with a one-line summary of what changed, and you can look back at an earlier version. Nothing runs until you choose **Create workflow**.
- **Blank**: one empty step to build on.
- **A starter**: **Weekly review** (an AI briefs the team every Monday morning and a person replies) or **Approval chain** (a person drafts, a person approves or denies, an AI posts the result). Starters need an AI representative on the team.
- **A template** someone saved earlier.

An empty team shows the two starters as one-tap buttons. An empty team also offers a few templates as one-tap starters. You can attach quests here if the workflow spans some. To keep a workflow you built as a template for next time, open the **...** options and choose **Save as a template**.

### Your first workflow, step by step

1. Open **Workflows** (menu, **AI Productivity**, **Workflows**) and choose the team in the scope button.
2. Tap **New workflow**. Give it a name, such as "Weekly review", and check the team in **For**.
3. Under **Start from**, describe what the workflow is for and who is involved so the AI drafts it, or pick a starter.
4. Read the draft ("Draft, not live yet"). Ask for changes in your own words, or tap a step to set **Who** and **When** yourself.
5. Tap **Create workflow**. A workflow made here is **Live** straight away: people with a step are notified and reminded when their step opens. Check the draft before you tap. To have people agree to their part first, start it as a draft from a quest's Workflows card (see [Agreement and going live](#agreement-and-going-live)).

ai_reps_intro.title: AI representatives
ai_reps_intro.text:
# AI representatives

An AI representative (an "AI rep") is your own AI counterpart in Quest. It is the version of [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) that acts as you: it carries your context, works in your voice, and can run work on your behalf. Everyone has one by default, and you can add more for different areas of your work.

If you are on a [team](/guide/teams), your default rep is also how teammates interact with "you" in AI: when someone brings your rep into a chat or hands it a task, it answers grounded in your context and preferences.

## Why AI representatives exist

An assistant that does not know your goals gives generic help, and one that acts without asking cannot be trusted with real work. A rep is built to avoid both. It carries your context and your way of speaking, it takes the first pass on work, and anything that needs a person comes back to you as one clear [ask](/guide/teams#asks-for-you) that you approve, decline or pass on. You stay the reviewer. The rep also learns from your corrections and your answers, so the help fits you more over time instead of staying generic.

## Who AI representatives suit

- **Someone with more to do than hours**, who wants a first draft or a first pass done before they look at it.
- **A person with distinct areas of life or work** (research, writing, coaching clients) who wants a differently tuned rep for each.
- **A team member whose teammates keep asking them for the same kind of reply.** Their rep can answer first, in their voice, from their context, and bring the decision to them.
- **Someone who wants to stay in control.** By default, changes to your Quest data ask you first (see [What a rep may do for you](#what-a-rep-may-do-for-you)).

If you only use Quest alone and never hand work to the AI, your automatic default rep is all you need.

## Quick start

1. Open the menu, expand **AI Productivity**, and under **Your AI** tap **My AI Representatives** (the same entry is on your Profile page under AI Productivity).
2. Tap **Create a rep**. Enter a **Name**, an **Area or specialty (optional)** such as "Fitness, Career, Mentoring", and **Behavior (optional)** for how the rep should speak and behave.
3. Tap **Save**. To chat with it, tap the rep name at the top left of a Quest AI chat and choose it, or @mention it in a team chat.
4. Correct it as you go: long-press a reply to give feedback, and answer its asks. It learns from both.

My AI Representatives is part of the AI Productivity features: available during the 31-day Quest AI trial and on the paid plans. On the Free plan you see a **Subscribe** page instead.

## Your default rep

You always have exactly one **default rep**. If you have never set one up, Quest creates it for you automatically the first time it is needed, named from your profile. The default is the rep that:

- represents you to others on your team, and
- conducts a chat or runs a task when no specific rep is chosen.

You can change which rep is your default at any time (see below).

- **Create another rep** for a specific area, for example a "research" rep and a "writing" rep, each with its own focus. Tap **Create a rep**. The form asks for a **Name**, an **Area or specialty (optional)** (it helps the right rep be chosen at the right time) and **Behavior (optional)**. A **Person-less rep** switch makes a standalone helper that is not tied to any person; leave it off to make your own rep.

- **Edit how a rep acts.** Give it a name, a short description of its area, and Behavior (instructions for how it should respond as you). Behavior can be at most 8,000 characters: keep it to who the rep is, how it speaks and its few standing rules.

science_intro.title: Science
science_intro.text:
# Science

Science is where you look at the evidence on any question: published research papers and first-hand accounts of human experience, from every field. [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) is for talking through your own quests and life. Science is for finding out what is actually known.

Open it from the navigation menu. It has three modes, shown as tabs at the top.

Direct finds matching papers and experiences instantly.

first_quest_why.title: Create your first quest: why creating a quest is so detailed
first_quest_why.text:
## Why creating a quest is so detailed

Creating a quest takes more than typing a goal into a box, on purpose. A quest is a big, long-term goal, and a goal like that is worth finding the best strategies for before you start. Generic advice cannot do that, because the right path depends on where you start, what you have already tried, and your time, budget, beliefs and limits. So Quest asks for the specifics once, and uses them in every step after.

In Quest's words, a quest is the specification of one intention. It is written down the way [ESOI](/esoi/) writes any intention: the end state you want, how you will know it is real, what is in the way, what you prefer and refuse, the strategies that could work, and the experiments and plan that carry them out. Each of the five steps collects one of those parts, and each says why it asks:

| Step | What it asks | Why it asks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Vision** | The end state you want, in one short sentence | Your vision drives every AI recommendation in Quest: the area of life, the strategy research, your experiments and your final plan. The clearer it is, the more tailored your results. |
| **Context: Measurable outcomes** | The numbers or checks that show your vision is real | Your vision becomes real when you can measure it. Each line becomes a Metric Quest tracks. |
| **Context: Current state** | Where you are now and what you have tried | It is your starting line. Quest reads it to find the problems your strategies address, so honest detail now saves guessing later. |
| **Context: Preferences** | The principles to honor and what you will not do | Your ideals are the principles every strategy must honor. Quest filters strategies against them so the ones you see fit you. |
| **Grounded Strategies** | Which problems are true and which strategies you keep | The step turns your current state into the problems your strategies address, then shows strategies grounded in research or in a library spec. You decide which to keep. |
| **Experiments** | Which small tests to run | Experiments turn each strategy into something you do and record, so the quest learns from your own results. |
| **Plan** | Which habits to keep and the target date | The plan turns your chosen strategies into milestones, goals and habits on your calendar. Starting with a focused set of habits you genuinely want to track is more effective than committing to everything at once. |

Specific beats inspiring: "reduce my anxiety by half" gives Quest something to measure and plan against, while "be calmer" does not.

**Do I have to answer everything?** No. The vision is the only thing Quest needs to begin. Each section of the Context step can be left light and filled in later (you can always add more detail from your quest dashboard), though the less you say, the more general the suggestions. Past that, Continue in Grounded Strategies needs at least one strategy you keep, and in Experiments you either choose at least one experiment to run or use **Skip experiments**. If you already know your plan and do not want the detail, make a quick quest instead.

core_reflections.title: Core concepts: reflections, period reviews and wisdom points
core_reflections.text:
## Reflections and period reviews

A **daily reflection** is a short end-of-day or start-of-day check-in where you plan the day and note how it went. A **period review** is a longer reflection for a week, month, quarter, or year. Reviews can suggest goals for the next period and, for measurable goals, show a **trajectory** that tells you whether you are on pace. See [Productivity workflow](/guide/productivity).

**Wisdom points** are what you earn for doing the work: completing habits and finishing goals and milestones. They are Quest's progress signal and they feed the way your quest's planet grows.

hand_off_setting.title: Productivity workflow: handing work to your assistant
hand_off_setting.text:
### Turn it on or off

On the trial and paid plans it is on unless you turned it off. To change it, open **Settings**, find the **AI Tasks** section and use the **Tasks for your AI** switch. Turning it off hides the "Tasks for your AI" field in your daily reflection and stops your AI taking tasks.

Tasks run on their own, not in a chain. For steps in a fixed order use a [Workflow](/guide/workflows), and for what happens when a task falls short of its goal see [Follow-up and ordered work](/guide/ai-tasks#follow-up-and-ordered-work).

**Can I give it a list of jobs in order?** Not as a chain of tasks. Put the order inside one request, or use a [Workflow](/guide/workflows).

habit_intro.title: Habits and custom tracking: what a habit is
habit_intro.text:
# Habits and custom tracking

A habit is something you repeat on a schedule: meditate each morning, practice piano for 45 minutes, read 30 pages, call a parent twice a month. You choose how Quest counts it (a yes or no, a number of times, an amount, or time on a clock), when it repeats, and whether it reminds you. Habits are free on every plan.

A habit is different from the other ways Quest keeps your data:

- **A plain collection** is a log you add to whenever you like, with no schedule, no reminders and no place on Today. See [Data Collections](/data-collections/#collections-habits-and-insights).

habit_reminders.title: Habits and custom tracking: reminders and alarms
habit_reminders.text:
## Reminders and alarms

**A reminder** is a notification at a habit's scheduled time. Every habit with a **Scheduled Time(s)** gets one, repeating on its days, and an Interval habit gets one at every interval inside its active hours (up to 24 a day). Reminders are scheduled by the Quest app on your device, so allow notifications when Quest asks, and on each phone or browser where you want them. On a phone the reminder has buttons: **Done**, **Started** and **Skip**, or **Start Timer** and **Skip** for a Timer habit, so you can log without opening Quest.

**Turning reminders off.**
- All habit and goal reminders: tap the bell in the header, then the gear to open the notification settings, and turn off **Habit & Goal Reminders**. The **Push Notifications** switch there silences them too.
- Alarms only: turn off **Alarm-Style Reminders** in the same settings. Habits with an alarm then send regular reminders instead, and each habit keeps its own alarm setting.
- One habit: switch **Habit active** off in **Edit Habit**. It leaves Today and stops reminding you until you switch it back on.

habit_points.title: Habits and custom tracking: how a habit counts toward progress
habit_points.text:
## How a habit counts toward your progress

- **Wisdom points.** Completing a habit earns wisdom points based on the time it takes: five minutes of effort is one point. **Complete** counts in full, **Partial** counts half, and **Skip** counts a tenth, which rounds to nothing for a short habit. A Timer habit uses the time you actually logged. Reaching a Frequency-Based target or a Timer goal in a period earns a bonus. See [Progress and wisdom points](/guide/quests-and-plans#progress-and-wisdom-points).
- **Your quest's progress.** A quest's completion counts its habits and goals together, so logging habits moves the percentage you see on the quest.
- **Your reviews.** Weekly to yearly [period reviews](/guide/productivity#period-reviews) show what share of your goals and habits you completed, and your habit totals. Quest can suggest a lighter schedule for a habit you log less than half as often as planned.
- **Your analytics.** Each habit's analytics page opens on where you stand for the period, with a **Habit Consistency** section for streaks and missed days.
- **Your metrics.** A measurable outcome can be calculated from a habit or a collection (a total, an average, a count, the latest value, a share of entries or a streak). See [Productivity workflow](/guide/productivity#period-reviews).

To track a habit privately, switch on **Do not count toward scores** under **Scoring**. The habit is logged as normal, but it earns no wisdom points and stays out of your period review stats.

mentee_faq.title: Mentors: common questions for mentees
mentee_faq.text:
### Mentee: common questions

**Do I need a subscription to use a mentor?** No. There is no subscription to a mentor. You add credit by card and it is spent only when a check-in takes place.

**What does it cost?** Each mentor sets their own prices as check-in tiers, so the price per check-in is shown before you request. On the Free and Quest AI plans a 5% service fee is added on top of the mentor's price; on Quest Guided there is no fee.

**Am I charged when I send a request?** No. You need enough credit for the tier you choose, but nothing is taken until a check-in is completed or confirmed.

**Can a mentor see all my quests?** No. A mentor sees only the quests you share with them, as View or Edit, and you can stop at any time.

**Does a mentor guarantee results?** No. A mentor advises and holds you accountable. You still own your quest and your decisions.

**How do I know a mentor is qualified?** Each mentor shows a verification badge from an AI read of their application (Strong, Pass or Not yet verified), and a profile with background and credentials. Use both.

**What if I run out of credit?** Your check-ins still happen. The payment is held until you add credit, and your mentor is told.

mentor_tiers.title: Mentors: check-in tiers
mentor_tiers.text:
#### Set your check-in tiers

Open the **Mentorship Dashboard** (in your profile, or **Open your mentor dashboard** from the Mentorship page). Under **Payouts, prices and tools**, open **Your check-in tiers**, tap **Add a tier**, and give each a name (up to 80 characters), a short description and a **Price per check-in (USD)** of at least $1. You can offer up to eight tiers. Tap **Save tiers**. Mentees pick a tier when they request you, and you receive the full price you set.

With no tiers saved, your invite link does not work and mentees cannot request you, unless you have set a price for a particular client.

mentor_earnings.title: Mentors: earnings and payouts
mentor_earnings.text:
#### Earnings and payouts

You set your own check-in tiers: named packages, each with one fixed price per check-in, so mentees choose a tier and never an amount. When you complete a check-in, or your mentee confirms one that took place outside the app, the tier's price for that session is added to your earnings as pending credit. Any service fee your mentee pays is added on top of your price and never reduces it. A one-off payment from a mentee, sent with a note, is added the same way. Pending credit becomes available after a short waiting period (currently 7 days), shown on each earning in the app. The waiting period exists so that a refund or dispute can cancel the earnings before they are paid out. If your mentee's payment has not come through yet, the check-in still completes and your earnings stay on hold until their payment settles. A platform fee, if Quest applies one, is taken when the earnings are recorded and never changes earnings already recorded.

Your balance (**Your credit**, in **Billing & Subscription**) shows what is pending, what is available, and your history of earnings and withdrawals in one place. **Your payouts** shows each completed check-in and where its payment stands (Pending, Held, Available, Paid, Failed). Available earnings can pay for your own mentorship or be withdrawn to your bank. To withdraw, tap **Set up payouts** (or **Finish payout set-up**) once, which opens the secure Stripe onboarding, then tap **Withdraw**. Withdrawals need a minimum amount (currently $2.00), and earnings below it keep building until they reach it. When payouts are switched on and your payout set-up is complete, Quest also sends available earnings automatically every few hours.

Payouts are switched on by Quest, not by you. Until they are, the app tells you "Payouts are not switched on yet. Your earnings are safe and keep building."

Payout set-up is not available in every country. If it is not available where you live, your earnings stay in your account, you can spend them on your own mentorship, and the app tells you that withdrawal is not available for your country.

mentor_faq.title: Mentors: common questions for mentors
mentor_faq.text:
### Mentor: common questions

**Do I wait for approval?** No. You are listed as soon as you submit. An AI scores your application in a minute or two. The Quest team may review low scores afterwards.

**Is the review done by a person?** The score is produced by AI and shown with a written reason. It does not approve or reject you. A person can look at a flagged profile, add a note, or hide it in an emergency, and writes the reason when they do.

**What does it cost to apply?** There is no charge to apply.

**Can I get paid through Quest?** Earnings from completed check-ins are recorded in your balance, and withdrawal to your bank goes through Stripe once Quest has payouts switched on. Quest cannot promise earnings, payout dates or a number of clients. Your prices and clients are yours to set.

**What fee does Quest take from me?** You receive the full price you set for each check-in. The mentee's service fee (5% on the Free and Quest AI plans) is added on top, not taken from you.

**Who can see my application?** Mentees see your profile, prices and score badge, not your documents or the reasons behind your score.

**Can I mentor and be mentored?** Yes. One account can do both, and the Mentorship page shows both.

**Do check-ins happen inside Quest?** Check-ins are scheduled in Quest and you mark each one complete. The conversation itself happens however you and your mentee agree (chat, a call, in person), and the format you prefer is shown on your profile.

calendar_intro.title: Calendar Sync: what it is
calendar_intro.text:
# Calendar Sync

Calendar Sync connects your real calendar to Quest, in both directions. Your existing events help Quest and its AI understand when you are actually free, and your Quest schedule can show up on your calendar alongside everything else in your life.

You manage it from **Settings > Calendar Sync**. There are two kinds of calendar connection, and you can use either or both: **Google Calendar** (a direct connection from Quest's servers to Google, on web and phone) and **device calendars** (the calendars on your phone, including Apple Calendar, phone only). The same screen also has an **Email** card for connecting your Google email read-only; that is a separate feature covered in [Quest AI: Email](/guide/quest-ai#email), not part of calendar sync. One link between them: when Quest AI proposes a goal from an email (an interview time, a deadline) and you approve it, it becomes an ordinary goal and Calendar Sync puts it on your calendar like any other goal; nothing reaches your calendar before you approve.

## Set up in four steps

1. Open **Settings > Calendar Sync**.
2. Under **Add an account**, connect Google (**Connect Google**) or, on a phone, **This device** (**Enable calendar access**).
3. Under **Connected accounts**, find the calendar and turn its switch **On**. Tap the row to open its settings.
4. Choose what it does: turn on **Show events on Quest and use for AI scheduling** to bring its events in, and **Add Quest schedule to this calendar** to write your schedule out (then turn on **Sync goals** and/or **Sync habits**).

The screen has four groups: **Connected accounts** (one card per Google account, your device and your email), **Add an account**, **Sync preferences** (the master switch) and **Scheduling links**.

**What a fresh connection does.** Nothing, until you choose. A newly connected calendar starts with both directions off, and **Sync goals** and **Sync habits** off too. Open its settings and turn on **Show events on Quest and use for AI scheduling** to bring its events in, and **Add Quest schedule to this calendar** to write your schedule out; after that, switch on **Sync goals** and/or **Sync habits** to say what gets written. The calendar's settings start with one plain sentence about what it does right now, and says "Nothing is written to this calendar yet" until you turn something on. Turning a paused calendar back on also starts with both directions off, though your other settings are kept.

calendar_settings.title: Calendar Sync: settings for each connected calendar
calendar_settings.text:
### Calendar to Quest

- **Show events on Quest and use for AI scheduling.** Brings events from this calendar into Quest. Switching it on also switches on **Create goals from calendar events**, right beneath it, because putting your events on Quest as goals is the point of the sync; turn that one off if you only want the calendar to show busy time. They appear on Today and Schedule alongside your goals and habits, the AI plans your day around them rather than on top of them, and your scheduling links will not offer a time they cover. An event your calendar left untitled comes in as "Untitled event", and one marked tentative still counts as busy time.
- **Create goals from calendar events.** On by default when you switch on Show events on Quest, and easy to turn off right beneath it. New events on this calendar become goals in Quest. An event that had already ended when you switched this on is never added, so turning it on does not fill Quest with the day's earlier events. If the event later moves or changes length in your calendar, the goal moves with it, unless you have already finished the goal; a goal you moved yourself in Quest stays where you put it until the event next changes. An event you delete or decline in your calendar leaves its goal in Quest for you to delete or finish. A recurring event with a simple daily or weekly pattern becomes a habit instead of a one-off goal; more unusual recurring patterns are left as calendar events (see Limitations below). Quest does not send its own reminder for a habit made this way, because the event it came from already reminds you on its own calendar and two alerts for one thing is one too many.
- **File new goals under.** Shown once Create goals is on. A dropdown that picks the quest the new goals go into (or No quest). It is separate from the Quest to Calendar quest scope, so changing one never changes the other.
- **Mark past calendar events as done.** Off by default; shown once "Create goals from calendar events" is on. When one of the events this calendar created has passed, Quest checks off the matching goal or habit for you, so the time you actually spent shows up in your category stats without you checking it off by hand. It only ever applies to goals created after you turned Create goals on, never to older ones.
- **Recurring events days ahead.** How many days ahead recurring events from this calendar are brought into Quest.

workflows_order.title: Workflows: steps in a fixed order
workflows_order.text:
- **After a step**: instead of a fixed time, start a chosen wait after another step (one with an arrow into this one) and last a chosen length, for example "Within 1 day, starting 2 days after Send the brief is done". Choose whether the wait starts when that step's time is over or when it is marked done; for "done" you also set the longest wait, so a step that is never finished does not hold things up forever. Until the other step is done, this step shows "Waits on Send the brief" instead of a time, and it gets its real time the moment that one is done. Choosing an upstream step also draws the arrow for you. It can start when the other step's time is over, or as soon as it is done, with a limit on how long to wait if it never is. A step timed this way repeats whenever the other one repeats.

**Does it cost anything extra?**

ai_reps_may.title: AI representatives: what a rep may do
ai_reps_may.text:
A rep acts as you, but only inside lines you can see and move.

**It may, on its own:**

- Take the first pass on a task or a goal assigned to you, and draft the reply it recommends when another person's rep hands you an ask.

- Add a note to a quest, record progress on a measurable outcome, and raise or track an ask for you.

**It asks you first, by default:** changes to your Quest data, such as editing a quest's fields, creating or deleting goals, or completing a quest, and anything that speaks for you outside Quest, such as an outbound email, which waits in your approvals for you to review and send. After you have approved the same kind of change five times in a row without turning one down, Quest AI can offer, as an ask, to do it without asking from then on, and it goes back to asking the moment you turn one down.

**It does not:** take a goal that nobody is assigned to, appear in an **Assigned to** list (a goal is always assigned to a person), or answer an ask in your name as if you had. Details of how to answer: [Answering an ask](/guide/teams#answering-an-ask).

which_feature_map.title: Which Quest feature helps with my goal: the map
which_feature_map.text:
# Which Quest feature helps with my goal?

Quest has many features, and you do not need most of them for any one goal. This page maps common goals and circumstances to the features that fit, and says why. Each row also gives a question worth asking when the circumstance is not clear. Quest AI can ask these back to you, and you can ask them of yourself.

A quest is the specification and plan for one big goal or intent. Almost every route below starts with one: see [Create your first quest](/getting-started/your-first-quest). Plans differ in what the AI covers: the free plan has no time limit, AI features are free for the first 31 days, and everything you made stays yours. See [Plans and pricing](/reference/plans).

## Quick map

| If your goal or situation is | Start with | Then add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A daily habit | [Habits and custom tracking](/guide/habits) | [Daily reflection](/guide/productivity#daily-reflection), reminders and alarms |
| A big, long-term goal | [Create your first quest](/getting-started/your-first-quest) | [Experiments](/guide/experiments#experiments-in-plain-words), [Period reviews](/guide/productivity#period-reviews) |
| A career change | [Life design](/guide/life-design) and a quest for the change | [Deep Inquiries](/guide/deep-inquiries), [Mentors](/guide/mentors) |
| Preparing for a race or an exam | A quest with a date and measurable outcomes | Timed or quantity [habits](/guide/habits), [Calendar Sync](/guide/calendar-sync) |
| Getting mentored | [Mentors](/guide/mentors#mentors-for-mentees) | Share your quest with the mentor |
| Becoming a mentor | [Mentors](/guide/mentors#mentors-for-people-who-mentor) | Inviting your own clients |
| Running a team | [Teams](/guide/teams) | [Workflows](/guide/workflows), [AI representatives](/guide/ai-representatives) |
| Too many things at once | [Life design](/guide/life-design) | Group by intent, [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) |
| Keeping records of something (sleep, spending, a project) | [Data Collections](/data-collections/) | Habits for the repeating parts |
| Capturing ideas as they come | [Insights](/guide/insights) | Voice capture, daily reflection |
| Working out what is true about a question | [Science](/guide/science), [Deep Inquiries](/guide/deep-inquiries) | Experiments on yourself |
| Getting help while you are busy | [AI Tasks](/guide/ai-tasks), [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) | [Autopilot](/guide/ai-tasks) |

which_feature_big_goal.title: Which Quest feature helps with my goal: big goals and dated events
which_feature_big_goal.text:
## Reach a big, long-term goal

**Fits when** the goal is large, unclear or matters a great deal to you.

- Create an AI-assisted quest. Creation is detailed because a big goal is worth finding the best strategies for before you start. See [why creating a quest is so detailed](/getting-started/your-first-quest#why-creating-a-quest-is-so-detailed).
- Run [experiments](/guide/experiments#experiments-in-plain-words) to find out which approach works for you.
- Hold a [period review](/guide/productivity#period-reviews) weekly or monthly so the plan stays true to what happened.

**Ask back:** What would success look like in a year? Do you already know your plan, or do you want help finding strategies? If you already know the plan, a quick quest is enough.

## Prepare for a race, exam or event with a date

**Fits when** a date sets the pace.

- Make a quest with measurable outcomes and a date.
- Track the training or study as [habits](/guide/habits): a timer for hours, a quantity for distance or pages, or sessions per week.
- Use [Calendar Sync](/guide/calendar-sync) so goals and busy times appear in one place.
- Period reviews show whether you are ahead, on pace or at risk.

**Ask back:** What is the date? Is it measured in time spent, a quantity, or sessions per week?

which_feature_unsure.title: Which Quest feature helps with my goal: too many goals or unsure
which_feature_unsure.text:
## Too many goals, unsure what matters

**Fits when** you have many quests and a feeling of being pulled in every direction.

- [Life design](/guide/life-design) groups quests under a few top intents.
- Ask [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) what to focus on, then use the daily reflection to choose today's goals.

**Can Quest help with my goal?** If the goal matters to you and has an end state you can describe, yes: that is what a quest is for. Start with the quest creation flow and the features above.

**What if I am not sure what I want?** Start with [life design](/guide/life-design). It asks short questions about what you want your life to be about.

which_feature_ai.title: Which Quest feature helps with my goal: AI help and teams
which_feature_ai.text:
## Run a team or an organization

**Fits when** several people share goals.

- [Teams](/guide/teams) give shared quests and **Asks for you**, the questions waiting on you.
- [Workflows](/guide/workflows) turn recurring work into steps, each with an owner and a time.
- [AI representatives](/guide/ai-representatives) let the AI act for a team member, within limits.
- [Delegates](/guide/delegates) let an assistant or partner answer your asks.

**Ask back:** Who owns each part of the work? Does it repeat on a schedule?

## Let the AI do part of the work

- Ask [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) in chat. On the Free plan chat answers questions about Quest from these docs; during the 31-day trial and on paid plans it also knows your quests.
- Delegate work from chat or the daily reflection: see [AI Tasks](/guide/ai-tasks). Task types include quest operations (such as creating goals and notes), web lookups, science questions, answers from Quest's own docs, and longer background work. [Which kind of AI task for what](/guide/quest-ai#which-kind-of-ai-task-for-what) shows how to ask for each.
- For several steps in a fixed order, build a [Workflow](/guide/workflows). Tasks do not chain into an ordered list on their own.
- If a task does not meet its goal, it retries within the same task and then ends as **Not fully done** or **Needs your input**; see [When the work is not finished](/guide/quest-ai#when-the-work-is-not-finished).
- Speak instead of typing with [Voice Mode](/guide/voice-mode).

account_assistant.title: Account settings: Tasks for your AI
account_assistant.text:
## Assistant (delegation)

In **Settings**, the **AI Tasks** section has a **Tasks for your AI** switch that turns delegating tasks to your AI on or off. It is on by default. When on, you can hand work to your AI from chat and from the daily reflection. See [Hand work to your assistant](/guide/productivity#hand-work-to-your-assistant).
